_comment: Container image pinning policy. Every third-party image and Dockerfile base image is pinned to a DIGEST, not a tag — a tag is a moving target, so `:latest` means you cannot say what you are running until you look. Digests make the stack reproducible and make an upgrade a visible, reviewable diff. BUT: pinning WITHOUT an update process is worse than :latest, because you silently freeze on a vulnerable image. That is what reviewBy exists for — scripts/image_policy_check.py FAILS once the date passes, the same forcing-function pattern as context/model-policy.json. See ai-standards/references/dependency-security.md.
_reviewBy_note: Monthly, not quarterly: the orchestration tier in this stack has a heavy critical-CVE record (n8n shipped multiple CVSS 9.4-10.0 RCEs in 2026). Re-resolve digests, read the changelogs, re-run the scan, then move this date.

images.risk: HIGHEST in the stack. Executes user-supplied workflow expressions by design, so arbitrary code execution IS the product and the attack surface is structural. 2026 CVEs incl. CVE-2026-21858 (CVSS 10.0 unauth RCE), CVE-2026-25049 (9.4 unauth RCE), CVE-2026-27495/27497 (9.4). Mitigated here by binding to 127.0.0.1 only and holding no repo mount.
images.verifiedNotVulnerable: 2.36.9 clears every published 2.x advisory floor (max floor 2.36.2, from the 2026-08-19 batch). Checked 2026-08-31 against the GitHub Security Advisory API for n8n-io/n8n, not a changelog. Trivy on this digest: 3 fixed HIGH (libcrypto3, libssl3, nodemailer), 0 CRITICAL.

images.risk: Low. stdlib only — no pip install, so no third-party dependency surface at all. Runs non-root with read-only mounts.
images.repinNote: CORRECTED 2026-09-17. The 2026-09-03 re-pin took Dependabot digests without checking what they were. The FROM lines carried a digest and no tag, so Dependabot tracked `:latest`: the pinned node digest was node:latest (Node 26.8.1, FULL Debian 13, 455 packages) and the python digest was python:latest (3.14.7, full Debian 13), while this record still said the tags below. Every check stayed green; security-scan then failed nightly from 2026-09-13 on 39 CRITICALs in ImageMagick/perl/LibRaw, packages a slim or alpine image never contains. The live containers were never rebuilt and ran the intended images throughout. FROM lines now name `tag@digest`, and image_policy_check fails any ref whose tag does not match this record. Verified: this digest is python:3.12-alpine as resolved 2026-09-17; Trivy with the CI flags reports zero CRITICALs.

images.where: router/, scrubber/, claude-runner/, gemini-runner/ Dockerfiles, and the node22 stage of capability-factory/Dockerfile.builder
images.risk: Router and scrubber are the privileged path — the router writes the audit ledger, the scrubber is the only holder of the PII vault. npm dependency surface is the supply-chain exposure here; see the lockfile rules in the lens.
images.repinNote: CORRECTED 2026-09-17. The 2026-09-03 re-pin took Dependabot digests without checking what they were. The FROM lines carried a digest and no tag, so Dependabot tracked `:latest`: the pinned node digest was node:latest (Node 26.8.1, FULL Debian 13, 455 packages) and the python digest was python:latest (3.14.7, full Debian 13), while this record still said the tags below. Every check stayed green; security-scan then failed nightly from 2026-09-13 on 39 CRITICALs in ImageMagick/perl/LibRaw, packages a slim or alpine image never contains. The live containers were never rebuilt and ran the intended images throughout. FROM lines now name `tag@digest`, and image_policy_check fails any ref whose tag does not match this record. Verified: this digest is node:22-bookworm-slim as resolved 2026-09-17 (Node 22.23.2, Debian 12); Trivy with the CI flags reports exactly one CRITICAL, CVE-2026-59873, restored to .trivyignore.

images.risk: Deliberately NOT firewalled (the research phase sniffs arbitrary APIs) and profile-gated off by default. Highest-privilege lane when running — start it explicitly and supervise it.

CI-only, never in the runtime stack. Pinned deliberately rather than using the marketplace trivy-action: a third-party GitHub Action runs arbitrary code with repo context inside a security-critical pipeline. Safe to pin — Trivy fetches its vulnerability DB at run time, so a pinned binary still sees fresh CVEs; only the scanner engine is frozen.

notPinned.why: Built locally from this repo. Their reproducibility comes from the pinned FROM digests above plus the committed source, so a tag is sufficient.

_pendingBumps_note: Version drift FOUND BY scripts/research_watch.py and deliberately deferred to the next review rather than bumped on the spot. Recorded so the deferral is a decision with a date, not a thing someone forgot. image_policy_check.py prints these on every run, so the queue cannot be missed while reading the policy it belongs to.

lastReview.verdict: NOT routine. The queued 2.30.7 -> 2.32.5 bump was superseded mid-flight by a security signal, exactly as the pendingBumps note said it would be if one landed.
lastReview.finding: n8n published advisory batches on 2026-08-05 and 2026-08-19. Against the GitHub Security Advisory API: 41 advisories affect the pinned 2.30.7 (27 high / 13 medium / 1 low), including expression-sandbox escapes to host RCE, a JavaScript task-runner VM escape, MCP path-traversal RCE and several credential-exfiltration paths. The QUEUED target 2.32.5 would still have left 27 of them open (17 high) — bumping to the scheduled version would have looked like remediation and delivered a third of it.
lastReview.action: Re-pinned to 2.36.9. Confirmed 2026-08-31 that n8nio/n8n:latest AND :stable both resolve to this exact digest, so it is the vendor's own designated stable release, not a conservative guess — 2.37.x is the pre-release line.
lastReview.scanEvidence: Trivy (aquasec/trivy 0.74.0), --severity CRITICAL,HIGH --ignore-unfixed: deployed 2.30.7 = 56 findings; candidate 2.36.9 = 3 (all HIGH, none CRITICAL). CI gates on CRITICAL, so the candidate passes.
lastReview.exposureNote: n8n binds 127.0.0.1 and [::1] only and sits on the internal agentnet, so most of these advisories need an already-authenticated session or a shared workflow editor. That lowers likelihood; it does not make sandbox-escape-to-RCE acceptable on the component that executes agent-authored workflows.
lastReview.allDigestsMoved: All five base images had been rebuilt since 2026-07-24 and were re-resolved, not just n8n.
lastReview.deployStatus: PIN DECLARED, CONTAINER NOT YET RECREATED — an n8n major-line upgrade runs one-way DB migrations against the n8n-data volume. See the runbook note before recreating.
lastReview.breakingChanges: NONE APPLICABLE. n8n's packages/cli/BREAKING-CHANGES.md has exactly one 2.x entry, 2.0.0 (npm removed from the n8nio/RUNNERS image), which we are already past and which does not apply: we run n8nio/n8n and do not extend it. 2.30.7 -> 2.36.9 crosses zero documented breaking changes.
lastReview.rollback: n8n documents no downgrade path and uses TypeORM forward-only migrations, so the ONLY rollback is restoring the n8n-data volume (40MB). Back it up before recreating the container; n8n's own upgrade doc does not mention this.

followUp.what: Took the Dependabot base-image bumps for node and python (PRs #16-#20) after scanning both proposed digests.
followUp.why: node f5d1cc4 ships tar 7.5.19, which REMOVES CVE-2026-59873 entirely — so accepting the bump deleted a .trivyignore exception rather than adding one. python 8edbf9e scans 0 fixed CRITICAL. n8n stays at 2.36.9: no published tag fixes CVE-2026-60002.
followUp.exceptionsNow: 1 (CVE-2026-60002, openssh, unreachable in this deployment), down from 2.
